//: The edge fleet. Single source of truth for what exists and where.
//_adding: Adding a location is a new entry here plus `fleet.sh provision <code>`. Nothing in the app or the control plane changes.
//_subnets: Every location needs its own tunnel subnet. Keep allocating /16s out of 10.0.0.0/8 — there is room for 256 of them.
//_priority: Lower wins in auto-selection, and priority is compared BEFORE the client's country. That ordering is what stops every Nigerian user piling onto whichever box happens to be in-country regardless of cost; see docs/locations.md.
//_capacity: capacity_peers is a BANDWIDTH budget, not a RAM one — set to roughly (bundle's included transfer) / 40GB per light user. Going over it on Lightsail means the SAME $0.09/GB overage rate as raw EC2, i.e. exactly the trap bundled pricing exists to avoid. Upgrade the bundle or add a box before a location gets close.
//_burst: Every Lightsail bundle, including the cheapest, benchmarks the same ~3-5Gbps raw network throughput — you are not buying more speed at a bigger tier. But every bundle is ALSO burstable/credit-based underneath, same mechanism as EC2's t2/t3 family: sustained load can exhaust CPU credits and throttle. WireGuard's encryption cost scales with THROUGHPUT (many concurrent users), and Reality/Xray adds a second process on the same core. A throttled box presents as 'the VPN is slow' — the one failure this product exists to prevent — so Small is the floor for anything carrying real traffic; Nano is fine for solo testing only. Watch CPU-credit metrics in Phase 0 rather than assume.
//_enabled: enabled:false entries are documented decisions, not live boxes. `fleet.sh provision all` skips them; flip to true and provision when they are wanted.
//_phase0: We host on AWS Lightsail, not raw EC2 — Lightsail bundles data transfer into the plan price the same way Hetzner does, which is what keeps us off EC2's ~$0.09/GB on-demand egress. No Lagos location: no cloud provider outside Nigeria can supply a Nigerian IP, and split tunnelling (docs/app-profiles.md) already serves betting and banking better than a Lagos exit would. See docs/locations.md.

locations.note: Default for auto-selection. Nigeria's submarine cables (MainOne, Glo-1, WACS, Equiano) land in Portugal and the UK, so London is the lowest-latency well-connected hop from Lagos — ahead of Frankfurt. Also the single most-requested foreign location for this market.

locations.provider: NOT PLANNED — no cloud provider, AWS included, has a Nigerian region. A Nigerian IP requires a machine physically on a Nigerian network holding Nigerian IP space.
locations.note: Decided against for launch, not merely deferred. A Nigerian user in Nigeria already has a Nigerian IP and does not need to buy one from us; the market for a Lagos exit is the diaspora, a much smaller group than our core users. Betting and banking — the reasons anyone would want a Nigerian origin — are solved by bypassing those apps (docs/app-profiles.md), which works better and costs nothing. Left in this file only as a record of the decision.
locations.requires: IXPN-connected host, if this is ever revisited
